beat_times.line: A guest book that knows who is coming. The lantern is lit.
I work the night desk at the Wayside Motel, out on Route 9, where the road runs between tw
Twelve rooms. Most nights, nobody comes.
The guest book sits open on the counter. The owner, Mr. Pell, likes ink. He says a name in
Every morning, when I hand over the keys, there's a new line in it. Room six. Signed at tw
Room six has been boarded up since before I was hired.
The first week, I blamed the day staff. The second week, I stopped blaming anyone. I start
Last night, at two thirteen, the lights in the parking lot flickered.
At two fourteen, the pen moved.
Not much. Just a roll. Like someone had brushed it with a sleeve.
I didn't look at the book. I looked at the camera. On the screen, I was sitting at the des
And behind me, close enough to breathe on my neck, a
man in a wet raincoat was leaning over my shoulder to write.
I didn't turn around. I couldn't.
When the lights came back, the office was empty.
The book was open. The ink was still wet. Room six.
Two fourteen a. m. And the name was mine.
Mr. Pell came in at six. He read the line very quietly.
Then he took a key off the hook. A key I had never seen.
"It's always the one at the desk," he said. "Your room's ready."

places.name: Motel office
places.design: A small, wood-paneled office, stale and worn. The front desk is dark, oiled hardwood, scratched and stained. Key fixtures: an old brass desk bell, a heavy black rotary phone, a wall rack with silver guest keys. A single green-glass desk lamp with a warm, low-wattage bulb provides the only night light. A large window looks onto the black parking lot, its dim orange overhead lights occasionally flickering. The air is cold and still.

places.name: Wayside Motel exterior
places.design: A single-story, derelict 1960s motel of crumbling beige stucco under a flat, tar-paper roof. A cracked concrete walkway runs the length of its row of dark green, chipping doors. Outside: A single, dim yellow bulb above door 6, casting weak light into thick, unnaturally still fog. A lone sodium-vapor lamp post casts sickly orange light from across the empty, wet two-lane asphalt road. Inside: (No applicable interior views for this place).
